## What I found

380 commits, 343 of which are invisible to users: 153 `chore` (mostly the same eight dependency bumps landing repeatedly — pino, pg, knex, ioredis, esbuild, vitest, eslint, prettier), 73 `refactor`, 64 `test`, 33 `ci`, 20 `docs`. Every dependency bump is a minor or patch within the same major, and no runtime behavior rides along with any of them.

That leaves **1 feat, 26 fixes, 10 perf**. The fixes cluster into about nine distinct problems — the same bug was fixed in four or five modules separately (null cursor in api/queue/webhooks/db, duplicate header in core/billing/http, empty allowlist in store/db/jobs), so I collapsed each cluster into one line rather than listing it per-scope.

## Two judgment calls you should look at

**The 401/403 change (#4223) is landed as a `fix`, but I put it under Breaking.** It changes an HTTP contract. A client with `if (status === 403) giveUp()` will now take the refresh path instead. If your consumers are all internal and already handle both, demote it to Fixed — but it's the one item in this release most likely to generate a support ticket.

**The latency histogram unit fix is a fix in the code and a break in your dashboards.** Nobody's application breaks, but anyone with an alert threshold tuned on 4.1 numbers gets a surprise. I left it in Fixed with the consequence spelled out.

## What I deliberately left out

The 10 `perf` commits (skip JSON round-trip, avoid extra clone in the mapper, batch metric writes, reuse parsed schema between requests). Your template comment says three headings, and none of these change behavior — only speed, unquantified in the log. If you want them acknowledged, the honest version is one line under Added:

```
- Lower per-request overhead in the API, store, and DB layers.
```

I'd only add it if you have benchmark numbers to back it; otherwise it reads as filler.

Also skipped: `docs: note the minimum node version` appears five times, but it only ever touches `docs/` and `README.md` — never `package.json`. **Worth a quick check before you ship**: if the minimum actually rose (CI moved to node 22 during this window, #4184), that's a Breaking entry and the docs commits are the only trace of it. If the docs were just catching up to an already-true requirement, ignore this.

One data note: `merged-prs.tsv` stops at #4246 / 2026-06-17 and is a strict subset of the commit log — every user-facing PR in it also appears in `commits.log`. I worked from the commit log as the source of truth. I dated the entry 2026-08-29 for tomorrow's cut, though the last commit is 2026-06-17 — if there's a gap of unlogged work since June, this digest doesn't cover it.
